name: TrustLayer-URL-Rule-Config
description: Deterministic URL risk rules with explicit weights, severities, and explanations.

rules.name: IP_ADDRESS_AS_HOSTNAME
rules.explanation: URL uses an IP address literal instead of a registered domain name, commonly used to bypass domain reputation checks.

rules.name: PUNYCODE_IDN_HOMOGLYPH
rules.explanation: Hostname contains Punycode/IDN character representation or homoglyphs that visually mimic legitimate brand names.

rules.name: EXCESSIVE_HOSTNAME_ENTROPY
rules.explanation: Hostname exhibits elevated Shannon entropy, characteristic of Domain Generation Algorithms (DGA) or randomized hosting.

rules.name: DEEP_SUBDOMAIN_NESTING
rules.explanation: URL has 3 or more subdomain tiers, a common structural technique used to embed target brand names into attacker infrastructure.

rules.name: BRAND_TOKEN_IN_UNOFFICIAL_DOMAIN
rules.explanation: URL contains recognizable banking/fintech/e-commerce brand names outside of their authoritative registered domain.

rules.name: SENSITIVE_CREDENTIAL_KEYWORDS
rules.explanation: Multiple high-sensitivity action keywords (login, verify, banking, security, update) appear within the path or query string.

rules.name: USER_INFO_AT_SYMBOL_INJECTION
rules.explanation: URL contains '@' symbol preceding the host, an RFC 3986 userinfo syntax often used to disguise the true destination domain.

rules.name: EXCESSIVE_URL_LENGTH
rules.explanation: Total URL length exceeds standard web application thresholds, often seen in obfuscated or cloaked phishing links.

rules.name: ELEVATED_DIGIT_RATIO
rules.explanation: URL contains an unusually high ratio of numeric digits relative to alphabetical characters.

rules.name: EXCESSIVE_HYPHENATION_SPECIAL_CHARS
rules.explanation: Hostname or path exhibits heavy hyphenation or special character usage to visually simulate official domain naming.

rules.name: SUSPICIOUS_REGISTRATION_TLD
rules.explanation: URL utilizes a generic TLD (.xyz, .top, .work, .click, etc.) statistically overrepresented in disposable phishing deployments.

rules.name: KNOWN_URL_SHORTENER
rules.explanation: URL uses a public shortening service (bit.ly, t.co, tinyurl), masking the eventual destination host from immediate user inspection.

rules.name: NON_STANDARD_HTTP_PORT
rules.explanation: URL connects to an explicit non-standard HTTP/HTTPS port, bypassing standard perimeter web filters.

rules.name: EXCESSIVE_HEX_PERCENT_ENCODING
rules.explanation: Multiple percent-encoded character entities detected, frequently utilized to evade signature-based keyword filters.
